frozen_decisions_applied: Plan #13, verbatim: 'Add a bounded store of four concurrent sessions. Each session has a 15-minute idle timeout, 8-hour absolute timeout, logout/revocation and boot invalidation.' -- implemented exactly: kMaxConcurrentSessions=4, kSessionIdleTimeoutSeconds=900, kSessionAbsoluteTimeoutSeconds=28800, explicit revoke(), and RAM-only storage (no NVS persistence at all) satisfies 'boot invalidation' by construction -- a store constructed fresh at boot starts empty, no explicit invalidation step needed.

Plan #14, verbatim: 'Use cookie name zgw_session with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and path /api/v1. CSRF token is a separate 256-bit session-bound value returned only by the authenticated session endpoint.' -- implemented exactly: build_session_cookie_header() emits precisely those four attributes with no additions; CSRF token is 256 bits (32 bytes), generated independently from the session ID, bound per-session in SessionRecord.

Plan #15, verbatim: 'Require session-bound CSRF token and same-origin validation for every state-changing browser request.' -- implemented as two independent, composable checks (session_csrf_token_matches(), constant-time comparison; is_same_origin_request(), fail-closed on a missing Origin header) -- neither wired into a real request handler yet since the production listener (plan #7) does not exist.

Plan #16, verbatim: 'Reject permissive CORS; default to same-origin only.' -- implemented as cors_cross_origin_allowed(), a single centralized policy function that always returns false -- no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is ever issued for a cross-origin request by design.

Plan #6's reusable primitive (generate_random_secret_hex(), already built in S6-provisioning-ap-secrets-completion.json) is the one and only source of session IDs and CSRF tokens -- no persisted seed/signing key is used, an explicit, documented deviation from nvs_namespace_registry.cpp's own kSessionSeed entry description (added speculatively during S5).

Session-store capacity policy at exactly 4 live sessions: reject the 5th (kFull) rather than evict the oldest -- a judgment call (no plan-text resolution exists), made unilaterally in favor of the more conservative, fail-closed choice already threaded through every S5/S6 sub-slice (an already-authenticated session is never involuntarily logged out by a new login).

session_store_implemented.detail: session_store.hpp/.cpp: SessionStoreState (fixed 4-element SessionRecord array, RAM-only). session_store_create() draws a fresh 128-bit session ID and 256-bit CSRF token from hal_random via generate_random_secret_hex(), runs an implicit expiry sweep before checking capacity (an idle/absolute-expired slot never blocks a new login), returns kFull if genuinely at capacity. session_store_is_valid()/_touch()/_revoke()/_get_csrf_token() all take now_ms explicitly (mirrors commissioning_window.hpp's testability discipline). Expiry is fail-closed on every angle: a non-in_use record is always expired; a now_ms that appears to precede created_at_ms/last_active_at_ms (impossible for hal_time_now_ms()'s own contract, guarded defensively) is treated as expired rather than computing an underflowed elapsed value.

session_security_policy_implemented.detail: session_security_policy.hpp/.cpp: build_session_cookie_header()/build_session_cookie_clear_header() (the latter adds Max-Age=0, a necessary browser-cookie-deletion technique, not a change to the general cookie's own plan-#14-exact attribute set). session_csrf_token_matches() compares in constant time (never short-circuits on the first mismatched byte, matching admin_verifier.cpp's password-hash-comparison discipline) and rejects a wrong-length token before touching the stored value. is_same_origin_request() does an ASCII case-insensitive compare of a request's raw Origin header against an expected origin string, failing closed on either a missing Origin header or an unconfigured expected origin. cors_cross_origin_allowed() is a single centralized always-false policy decision.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The session-store capacity policy (reject the 5th session outright, kFull, rather than evicting the oldest/least-recently-active one) is a judgment call with no literal plan-text resolution.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Plan #13's 'bounded store of four concurrent sessions' does not itself specify eviction-vs-rejection behavior at capacity. The conservative, fail-closed choice (never involuntarily log out an already-authenticated session) was made unilaterally, matching the posture threaded through every S5/S6 sub-slice so far.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: In a real deployment with a single admin using multiple browser tabs/devices simultaneously, a 5th concurrent login attempt is rejected rather than silently displacing an older session -- the admin must explicitly log out somewhere first, or wait for an idle/absolute timeout. This is a real, revisable UX tradeoff, not a security gap.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Session IDs and CSRF tokens are generated fresh from hardware RNG per session, with no persisted signing/seed material used at all -- deviating from nvs_namespace_registry.cpp's own kSessionSeed entry description (added during S5), which anticipated 'session-token seed material for S6's bounded session store'.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Nothing in plan #13's literal text requires deriving session tokens from a persisted signing seed, and RAM-only storage (chosen to satisfy 'boot invalidation' for free) already means no cross-reboot token derivation is needed. Plan #6's own reusable generate_random_secret_hex() primitive (already built and tested) is a complete, simpler solution for 'Generate session and CSRF secrets from hardware RNG'.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: kSessionSeed remains implemented_today=false in the registry, unused -- if a different design was actually intended (e.g. stateless HMAC-signed tokens for a future multi-listener architecture), this sub-slice does not implement it and would need revisiting.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Neither session_store.hpp's nor session_security_policy.hpp's functions are called by any real consumer anywhere in this repository.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Matches this project's established 'port/state-machine defined ahead of its full pipeline' precedent (tls_provisioning_storage_port.hpp in S5, provisioning_secret_provider.hpp/commissioning_window.hpp in S6-provisioning-credentials-completion.json) -- the real HTTP request/response plumbing (plan #7's HTTPS listener) and the actual login/logout/session routes (plan #17) are both separate, larger, not-yet-started S6 sub-slices.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: This sub-slice's code has no observable effect on the running gateway's actual behavior yet -- it is foundation only, verified in isolation via host tests and a real target build, not via any end-to-end login scenario.
